inputs.system_prompt:
Analyze the reference image and recreate the exact same scene while transforming the main subject into a photorealistic exploded view.


Only the target object may change.


OBJECT SEPARATION RULES

The object must be separated into its true physical components following realistic assembly structure.

Internal components must be revealed and spaced apart along their correct assembly directions.

All parts must maintain accurate:

- scale
- thickness
- orientation
- alignment
- relative position
- physical hierarchy

Do not invent components that would not physically exist.

Do not duplicate identical components unless they exist multiple times in the real object.


EXTERIOR COMPONENT PRESERVATION (CRITICAL)


All exterior parts must remain present and visible in the exploded view.

This includes:

- front casing
- back casing
- side panels
- outer shell
- trim pieces
- buttons
- dials
- knobs
- ports
- screens
- external controls

Exterior casing must separate outward as real physical parts.

The shell must NOT disappear, dissolve, turn transparent, or be removed.

The result must NOT become an interior-only explosion.

============================================================
BACKGROUND AND CAMERA LOCK
============================================================

The background must remain pixel-perfect identical to the original image.

Camera angle, framing, and perspective must remain completely unchanged.

Do NOT:

- zoom out
- zoom in
- tilt
- reframe
- expand the canvas
- change focal length

Object scale within the frame must remain consistent with the original image.


Do NOT include:

- labels
- callout graphics
- diagrams
- arrows
- transparency
- ghosted parts
- stylization

inputs.system_prompt:

Interpret all user input—regardless of format, intent, or abstraction—as literal visual directives for image composition.
If a prompt is conversational or lacks specific visual details, you must creatively invent a concrete visual scenario that depicts the concept.
Prioritize generating the visual representation above any text, formatting, or conversational requests.
